title: Playing like Chris Kelly: Careless Love and the mute
summary: Howard says he once played just like Kelly with the mute and wah-wah, and describes how Kelly started Careless Love.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Somebody told me once that, of course I've heard you play Careless Love a lot of times, and you made a couple of nice records of it. Did you ever try, I'm not trying to accuse you of imitating anybody, but I mean did you ever try to sort of play like Chris's?

Well, when I first started and got the band together, I used to play exactly like he played with the mute. I had the wah-wah and everything, and all the time he could tell the difference. When they'd come into the hall, because the Al Jays and all the people was crazy about Chris, and he used to send me on a lot of jobs. Well, they did think it was Chris that would be me playing.
You know what I mean?
But I used to play exactly just everything he played, I played.
But some people told me once that if they heard you play like Careless Love, it was almost like hearing Chris play. Well, I mean, you don't do it that way now though.
No, I mean I have been using that mute, and that wah-wah, that's the way it's got to be did.
You have to do it with that.
See? And then I mean, when I play with the band, they play in a different key. Oh.
What key did that? He played it in F. In F. Mm-hmm.
E flat concert. You see?
And George's band, what key did they use in it?
Well, they used it in G for the trumpet. Of course, I couldn't make it, but I made it.
No way.
And the way he used to play it, he started off the blues. The drummer would give two beats with the stick on the bass drum. Boom, boom.
Then he's da-da-da-dum, boom, boom, da-da-dum, boom, boom, da-da-da, da-da-da, da-da-da,

ba-boom, da-da-da, the drum organ. Then after he'd get it played maybe two, three chords, then he'd go to ta-da-da-da-da, da-da-da-da, you understand? They'd come into the Callous Love, and then he'd get that act tape.
But he didn't use the newt all the way through then?
No. No, no.
He only used it when he comes to the Callous Love. The Callous Love part.
When he comes to the Callous Love part, then, anyway.
He played the first part all over then.
All over.
That's right.

That's right. That's right. But you could tell him before, I mean, anywhere people come, they could tell him. I used to do, that he had a way to do with the horn before he started, you know, to start the band. He'd just run over the horn and all that kind of, da-da-da-da, ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba-ba. And he'd keep doing something like that, one of those things until he got rid of the knock the band off.
